Radius of a nucleus of mass number 64 is 4.8 Fermi. Find atomic mass number of nucleus of radius 4 Fermi.
(1) 48
(2) 37
(3) 54
(4)

steps:
Density of nucleus is constant
$$\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \frac{\text { mass }}{\text { volume }}=\frac{\text { Atomic number }}{R^{3}}=\text { constant } \\
\therefore \frac{A_{1}}{R_{1}^{3}}=\frac{A_{2}}{R_{2}^{3}} \\
\Rightarrow \quad A_{2}=\left(\frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}}\right)^{3} A_{1} \\
\Rightarrow \quad A_{2}=\left(\frac{4}{4.8}\right)^{3} 64 \\
\Rightarrow \quad A_{2}=37
\end{array}$$

6. The eccentricity of hyperbola $x^{2}-y^{2} \operatorname{cosec}^{2} \theta=5$ is $\sqrt{7}$ times of eccentricity of ellipse $x^{2}+y^{2} \operatorname{cosec}^{2} \theta=$ 5 then $\theta$ is where $0<\theta<\frac{\pi}{2}$
(1) $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$
(2) $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$
(3) $\theta=\frac{\pi}{-3}$
(4) $\theta=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$

Ans. (1)
Sol. Let $\mathbf{e}_{1}$ eccentricity of ellipse and $\mathbf{e}_{2}$ is eccentricity of hyperbola
$$\begin{array}{l}
e_{1}=\sqrt{1-\sin ^{2} \theta}=\cos \theta \\
e_{2}=\sqrt{1+\sin ^{2} \theta}
\end{array}$$
$\mathrm{e}_{2}$ is $\sqrt{7}$ times of $\mathrm{e}_{1}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\sqrt{1+\sin ^{2} \theta}=\sqrt{7} \cos \theta \\
1+\sin ^{2} \theta=7 \cos ^{2} \theta \\
2=8 \cos ^{2} \theta \\
\cos ^{2} \theta=\frac{1}{4}, \quad \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2}, \quad \cos \theta=\frac{-1}{2} \text { (rejected) } \\
\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}
\end{array}$$

Ans. (9)
Sol. $\quad \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=(((\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} . \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}-(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} . \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}) \times \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \times \hat{\mathrm{j}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=((\vec{b}-2 \vec{a}) \times \hat{j}) \times \hat{j} \\
=((\vec{b}-2 \vec{a}) \cdot \hat{j}) \hat{j}-(\vec{b}-2 \vec{a})(\hat{j} \cdot \hat{j}) \\
=((11 \hat{i}+2 \hat{k}) \cdot \hat{j}) \hat{j}-(\vec{b}-2 \vec{a}) \\
=-(\vec{b}-2 \vec{a})=2 \vec{a}-\vec{b}=-11 \hat{i}-2 \hat{k} \\
